SORTH third-party source delivery asset

This file describes THIRD-PARTY-SOURCES.tar.gz prepared by
project_root/tools/prepare_release_sources.py. Preparation does not publish it,
verify durable recipient access, clear redistribution rights, or establish that
any final SORTH binary contains exactly these inputs. It is not legal certification.

CONTENTS
- Original, byte-preserved Qt 6.11.2 qtbase, qtsvg, qtimageformats and
  qttranslations source archives, including their original licenses, embedded
  third-party sources, editable translations, configure/CMake scripts and changes.
- Original PyQt6 6.11.0 and PyQt6-sip 13.12.0 source archives with their licenses.
- Original Mesa 11.2.2 and LLVM 3.6.2 source archives and licenses, conservatively
  delivered as version candidates. Exact supplier configuration, patches and
  final component mapping for the retained Mesa DLL remain unresolved.
- Original Qt supplier build configuration, feature headers and SBOMs, selected
  by exact paths and SHA-256 from the pinned official Windows MSVC packages.
- Pinned wheel metadata and the exact installed Core/Gui/Widgets interface
  definitions and configuration. The two observed module include-list ordering
  differences are preserved by including the complete installed definitions.
- Inventory-named repository notices, including editable MPL Public Suffix List
  source and its Qt generator. Upstream original notices are not rewritten.
- Input provenance, a scoped supplier correspondence matrix and SHA256SUMS.

No supplier wheel, executable, DLL, Microsoft runtime, or research-machine script
is delivered as an outer bundle member. Some original upstream source archives
may contain upstream prebuilt/source-test assets; the archives are preserved
unmodified, not installed or executed. In particular PyQt-builder's sdist, which
contains Microsoft DLLs, is deliberately not downloaded or redistributed here.

BUILD CONTEXT
Qt's supplier config_*.opt and config_*.summary files and SPDX build annotations
record the actual public supplier settings. Source SBOMs are included where the
supplier provided them. They describe CMake 3.30.5 and MSVC 19.44.35227.0. Original
supplier machine paths in these public files are provenance and must be adapted
to local paths; they are not paths from the SORTH developer or release machine.
Read Qt's versioned Windows source-build guidance together with these files:
https://doc.qt.io/qt-6.11/windows-building.html
Build qtbase first, then retained add-on modules against that Qt installation.
Use the original archive build/install scripts and review platform prerequisites.
No source build or bit-identical reproduction is claimed by this packager.

PyQt6's WHEEL metadata identifies pyqtbuild 1.19.1. Installed .toml files identify
SIP 6.15.3, SIP ABI 13.8, Windows/Qt_6_11_0 tags and disabled features. The PyQt
source archive includes project.py, pyproject.toml and original SIP definitions.
Those tags do not prove the exact Qt SDK patch used to compile the wheel. Use
upstream sip-build/PyQt build guidance, the source configuration and preserved
installed interface definitions when adapting a build. Unmodified generally
available build tools are not claimed to be bundled here.
https://www.riverbankcomputing.com/static/Docs/PyQt6/installation.html
https://www.riverbankcomputing.com/static/Docs/sip/

EVIDENCE AND LIMITS
The supplier matrix compares the pinned official PyPI wheel against official Qt
supplier files for the prior retained-path selection: 20 Qt PE paths match, and
253 overlapping DLL/QM files match, including 217 translations. These are prior
supplier comparisons, not a comparison to the eventual SORTH release artifact.
Source SBOM comparison found no implementation/build-script discrepancy in the
three modules with supplied source SBOMs after LF/CRLF normalization; .tag and
Git-only metadata exceptions are recorded in the matrix's limitations. The
translations package supplies binary SBOMs but no separate source SBOM.

Qt/PyQt and third-party license alternatives remain alternatives. Inclusion of a
license does not select it or grant extra rights. PyInstaller's original preserved
bootloader exception should be applied only to its stated combined-executable
scope; it does not license modified/uncombined tools generally. This source asset
does not establish rights for the separately reviewed seven Microsoft runtime
files, replace their downstream terms, or authorize a public binary release.

RELEASE DELIVERY
Publish this exact asset with the selected binary only after the remaining gates
are resolved and publication is authorized. Deliver the separate exact SORTH
source_commit archive with build/packaging scripts and project license alongside
it; a link to mutable main is insufficient. Publish SHA-256 and clear source
access directions beside the binary, retain access, and verify downloaded assets.
Check all final retained native/Python components, including actual PyQt and
translation membership, notices, and any applicable shared-library replacement
and installation-information conditions. A source preparation CI artifact alone
is temporary evidence, not the final recipient-facing delivery strategy.

REPRODUCTION
From project_root with Python 3.12+ and trusted system 7z or 7zz available:
  python tools/prepare_release_sources.py --output build/release-sources/THIRD-PARTY-SOURCES.tar.gz
Use --cache-dir for an existing download cache and --offline to require it.
Each cached and fetched file must match the committed exact size/SHA-256.
The Qt origin master.qt.io is used directly to avoid unpinned third-party mirror
redirects. All redirects are rejected. The packager never executes vendor code;
7-Zip only lists and streams exact selected files to stdout. Original source
archives are inspected without extracting them. Unexpected links, traversal,
duplicates, missing selections and unbounded data cause failure.

Member names are sorted, ownership/modes/timestamps are fixed, and gzip has no
filename and a zero timestamp. Repeated runs under the same Python/zlib toolchain
produce identical bytes; compression implementations across toolchain versions
may differ. Every included file except SHA256SUMS has an internal SHA-256 entry.
The CLI prints the outer asset's SHA-256, byte size and explicit incomplete gates.
